LOT_INFO: Lot S97, Saturday, August 16th, //, 1951 Ferrari 212 Export Touring Barchetta, Pebble Beach Winner with Wayne Obry Restoration, Iconic Touring Ferrari for a Gentleman and Lady

ENGINE: 2563cc/147 HP V-12

MODEL: Ferrari 212 Export Touring Barchetta

HIGHLIGHTS: S/N 0136E, 1 of 8 212 Exports finished in Carrozzeria Touring’s Barchetta-style Superleggera bodywork, The 25th of 28 212 Exports built, The 212 Export had an 88-inch wheelbase chassis, Displayed at the Paris Salon in October 1951 as part of the Ferrari display, Sold to Irish racer Robert Baird following the Paris Salon, Baird immediately entered it in the Tourist Trophy race at Dundrod, finishing 6th overall in the 3.0L class, Baird campaigned it in the British Isles for the following two years before selling it to a South American owner, 0136E appeared in the Grand Prix of Rio de Janeiro in 1954 and the 1000kms of Buenos Aires in January 1956, Several years later, it was discovered in Uruguay by a British Ferrari enthusiast and shipped to Leicester, England, Around 1976, it was restored by Donald Nelson of Leicester and fitted with a 250 GT engine and 275 MM-style hood, Under Nelson’s ownership, 0136E appeared at Christie’s International Historic festival at Silverstone and the International Ferrari Concours d’Elegance in Monterey, California, Jack and Kingsley Croul purchased 0136E in 1999, In 1999, the Crouls drove 0136E in the Italia Classica rally, The following year, the Crouls drove the 212 Export in the Mille Autunno, Comprehensively restored by the renowned Wayne Obry of Motion Products Inc. in Wisconsin in 2012-2013, During Obry’s restoration, 0136E was reunited with its original Colombo engine and the hood scoop was returned to its original configuration, In May 2013, 0136E was invited to the Concorso d’Eleganza at Villa d’Este on the shores of Lake Como in Cernobbio, Italy, In August 2013, the Ferrari was invited to the Pebble Beach Concours d’Elegance, where it won First Prize in Class M-2, In January 2014, 0136E was awarded Platino at the 2014 Cavallino Classic in Palm Beach, Florida, 212 Export 88-inch wheelbase chassis, Original 2563cc/147 HP Colombo V-12 engine, Single 36DCF dual throat Weber downdraft carburetor, 5-speed manual gearbox, Live rear axle, Transverse leaf spring front suspension with unequal length upper and lower A-arms, Rear longitudinally mounted semi-elliptical leaf spring suspension, 4-wheel Alfin drum brakes, Borrani wire wheels

LOT_INFO: Lot S49, Saturday, August 16th, //, 1930 Cadillac Series 452 V-16 Sport Phaeton, Formerly Part of the Otis Chandler Collection, 452 CI V-16, 3-Speed, 1 of 17 Known to Exist

ENGINE: 452/175 HP V-16

MODEL: Cadillac Series 452 V-16 Sport Phaeton

HIGHLIGHTS: Formerly part of the Otis Chandler Collection, 1 of 85 Sport Phaetons built for the V-16 chassis for the 1930-1931 production model run and 1 of 17 known remaining examples, The Sport Phaeton featured a windshield mounted directly behind the front seat that could be raised and lowered with a hand crank, Delivered new by the Towell Cadillac Company of Cleveland to Perry Williams Harvey, It was later owned by Bennett Hammond of Brandy Flip Farm in Nicasio, California, Joseph Runyan of Pasadena purchased the car from Runyan in 1952, purportedly for $25, It had been abandoned on the Hammond property and they were thrilled to get it out of their way, Runyan then spent $2,500 on a restoration, which included hand-rubbed paint applied under a backyard shade tree, Featured in Roy Schneider’s "Sixteen Cylinder Motorcars" and in Maurice Hendry’s "Cadillac, Standard of the World: A Complete History" as well as a feature article in the October 1967 issue of "Car Classics", Runyan retained ownership of the Cadillac for the remainder of his life, starting another restoration in the early 1990s, which was completed shortly before his passing in 1995, It was at this time that the color was changed to Bottle Green, It was purchased from the Runyan family by noted collector Otis Chandler, who refreshed the restoration and subsequently won 2nd in Class at the Classic Car Club of America Grand Classic in July 1997 with a score of 95.25, It was later invited to be shown at the Pebble Beach Concours d’Elegance, where it received 3rd in class in 1998, The V-16 remained in the Chandler collection and was purchased by Keith Crain in 2006 after his passing, A mechanical service was performed, a new top installed and six new tires were fitted in 2020, It was professionally detailed prior to being shown at the 2021 Amelia Island Concours d'Elegance, CCCA Full Classic, 452 CI OHV V-16 engine rated at 175 HP at 3,400 RPM, engine no. 702515, Dual updraft carburetors, 3-speed manual transmission, 4-wheel mechanical drum brakes, Front beam axle with semi-elliptical leaf springs, Green and chrome wire wheels with Whitewall tires, Live rear axle with semi-elliptic leaf springs, Radiator stone guard, Dual side mount spares with accessory mirrors, Dual horns, Luggage rack with color-keyed trunk, Engine-turned dashboard
